free_tier.stated: 250 MB max data size on Free; 500K commands per month; 10 GB bandwidth/month
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: Free DBs minted anonymously are DELETED after 3 days unless claimed.

egress.terms: Free up to 10 GB per month on the Free plan (~333 MB per day), followed by metered bandwidth billing on paid tiers.

tooling: redis-cli over TLS, any Redis client, plus a body-style REST API (`POST` a JSON array command). Verified live: a free database can be minted with no signup via `POST https://upstash.com/start-redis` with an `Idempotency-Key` header.
chaining: Free tier is 1 database per account (pricing table: 'Max databases | 1'). 250 MB x N accounts. The command quota, not storage, is the wall: 500K commands/month = 16,667/day, and each GET returns at most 10 MB (verified), so max read throughput is 16,667 x 10 MB = 167 GB/day. 3x short of 500 GB/day even with a mythical 250 MB dataset read 667 times a day.
limits_note: 250 MB data; 10 MB max request size (LIVE-VERIFIED: a 20 MB SET returned 'ERR max request size exceeded. Limit: 10485760 bytes'); 100 MB max record size listed but the 10 MB request cap binds first; 10,000 max cmd/sec; 500K commands/month; 1 database

reliability_note: Works and is fast; the killer is the command meter. Every GET, SET, EXISTS, and even pipelined command counts. Operational commands (PING, AUTH, INFO, CONFIG, SELECT, COMMAND, RESET, QUIT) are explicitly not charged. Free DBs minted anonymously are DELETED after 3 days unless claimed.

evidence.proved: 'Free | $0/month | 250 MB | 10 GB' (Max Data / Max Bandwidth); FAQ: 'Free tier includes 250MB data size and 500K commands per month.'; 'Max databases | 1'
probe: POST (Idempotency-Key header) -> 200, credentials returned, 'Expires: 2026-10-24 (3 days from creation)'

probe: SET of a 1,000,000-byte value -> {"result":"OK"}; GET -> 1,000,013 bytes returned; STRLEN -> 1000000; 9 MB and 10,000,000-byte SETs also OK; a 20 MB SET -> {"error":"ERR max request size exceeded. Limit: 10485760 bytes"}

probe: INFO memory on the freshly minted free DB -> maxmemory:67108864 (64 MB), maxmemory_policy:noeviction — i.e. the anonymous/agent database is provisioned at 64 MB, well under the advertised 250 MB
arithmetic: 500,000 commands/month / 30 = 16,667 commands/day; x 10 MB max request = 167 GB/day ceiling. At a realistic 1 KB per command it is 16.7 MB/day — 30,000x short of 500 GB/day.
